$comment: RECORDED GREETINGS (D263). The boot line, pre-recorded, so first contact is not a local TTS voice.
Rendered in ElevenLabs on the voice named below; normalised to -16 LUFS to match the ad VO master.
KEYED BY THE LINE'S EXACT DISPLAY TEXT, AND NEVER BY INDEX. That is the whole safety property of
this file: persona.json's boot list is ORDERED for rotation (rule 4) and somebody will reorder it,
and an index-keyed manifest would then SAY one sentence while the transcript SHOWS another. An
unmatched line is not an error - it simply falls through to Piper, which is why the offline set
needs no entry here and why adding a greeting cannot break this file.
`renderText` is what was SENT to ElevenLabs and must never be shown to a user: `Mattick` forces
MAT-ik (rhymes with attic), because eleven_v3 mispronounced the name inconsistently on short
lines. persona.json carries the real spelling; `text` below must match it character for character.
NO VISEME TIMELINE IS NEEDED, and the brief that asked for one was wrong about this build. The
avatar's own manifest says "'talk' is the fallback when no viseme stream is bound", and
matic-avatar.css animates that mouth (`matic-talk 0.42s infinite`), switching it off only under
`.mav[data-visemes]`. So a recording plays against Claude Design's designed fallback - a generic
talking mouth, not a shut one - which is the same path `say()` already takes when Piper fails.
Real lip-sync would still be better, and it needs forced alignment; it is not a prerequisite.
THE SEAM IS THE COST, AND IT IS THE OPEN QUESTION. Matic introduces itself in this voice and
continues in Piper's `en_US-amy-medium`. Set `enabled` to false to hear the alternative: every
line goes back to Piper and nothing else changes. That toggle IS the experiment - nobody had
heard the seam when the four options were written down.
Only lines with no capability word and no outcome claim may be recorded, same as every persona
line; and a line D249 would redact may never be recorded, because a fixed file cannot be
rewritten before it is spoken. Both are asserted in test/recorded-speech.test.mjs.
loudness: -16 LUFS, two-pass loudnorm linear=true, TP ceiling -1.5 dBTP

lines.text: Hey, I'm Matic. What I can handle, I'll handle. What I can't, I'll get to someone who can.
lines.renderText: Hey, I'm Mattick. What I can handle, I'll handle. What I can't, I'll get to someone who can.

lines.text: Hi, I'm Matic. Tell me what you need in your own words.
lines.renderText: Hi, I'm Mattick. Tell me what you need in your own words.

lines.text: Hi, I'm Matic. Say what's going on, and I'll take it from there.
lines.renderText: Hi, I'm Mattick. Say what's going on, and I'll take it from there.
